extracted.intended_audience: research administrators, higher-education compliance officers, policy historians, and federal grants managers
extracted.subtask_short: history of OMB Circular A-110 revision
extracted.subtask_description: A historical analysis of the development and revision of OMB Circular A-110 via the COGR Subcommittee (1976–1979), aimed at extracting lessons for research administration practice and federal policy formation. Focuses on practitioner influence, paperwork/cost reduction, and standardization versus institutional diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility for research administrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Research administrators needed flexibility and reduced paperwork and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subcommittee adopted the philosophy that research administrators needed flexibility and reduced paperwork and costs; this principle guided efforts to shape A-110 revisions so administrators could focus on core duties rather than compliance burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization without stifling diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal principles needed standardization without stifling the diversity that is the strength of American higher education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should create common standards but be careful not to impose rigid one-size-fits-all rules that undermine institutional variety and strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce burdens associated with property and procurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempts were made to reduce the burdens associated with property and procurement matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific attention in revisions was given to easing administrative burdens in property management and procurement tied to federal awards, recognizing these as significant cost and workload drivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value practitioner expertise and erudition
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal counterparts respected and cooperated with the erudition of the subcommittee's members about issues that curtailed research administrators from their duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In rulemaking and revision processes, incorporate the practical knowledge of experienced research administrators to identify real-world compliance pain points and workable solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize reducing costs of accounting for federal awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies should avoid measures that threaten to raise costs of accounting for federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposed requirements for their administrative cost impact and seek alternatives that accomplish oversight without disproportionate accounting burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure practitioner-led advocacy for revision
rubrics_metrics.description: The subcommittee's goal was to ensure revision of the OMB Circular A-110 after it was first published on July 1, 1976.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active, organized advocacy by practitioner groups (e.g., COGR subcommittees) is an effective mechanism to initiate and shape regulatory revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate research administrators' common sense and experience in policymaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The subcommittee's successes are causes for celebration and recognition that research administrators' common sense and experience count in shaping federal principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy development should explicitly recognize and leverage on-the-ground administrative experience as a source of practical policy improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-stakeholder communication and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties in the research effort--scientists, researchers of every discipline, executives, and controllers--need to get this message to continue the necessary work of transforming the vision for the public good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained communication among faculty, administrators, financial officers, and policymakers is necessary to maintain reforms that balance oversight with research facilitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use historical analysis to inform continual evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: This article uses a critical era in the history of research administration to retrieve a new and deeper understanding of A-110 and why the experiences of research administrators and their networks are critical in shaping continual evolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical case studies of policy formation can surface lessons and precedents that inform current regulatory reform efforts and stakeholder strategies.
